```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Root locator + dual-load idiom shared with the get-started vignette: the
# source tree (check and site-build contexts) loads through pkgload; a bare
# installed package (reader-side) loads through library().
.pkg_root <- function() {
  for (dd in c(".", "..", "../..")) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "DESCRIPTION")) &&
        file.exists(file.path(dd, "R", "treatment-report.R"))) return(normalizePath(dd))
  }
  NA_character_
}
PKG <- .pkg_root()
if (!is.na(PKG) && requireNamespace("pkgload", quietly = TRUE)) {
  suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(pkgload::load_all(PKG, quiet = TRUE,
                                                      export_all = TRUE)))
} else {
  library(msuiter)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Every downstream claim — an extracted signature, a fitted exposure, a
presence call — inherits the quality of the catalog it came from. The QC
faces inspect that inheritance *before* the analysis: mutation burden,
strand artifacts, flat "pseudosignature" contributions from technical
processes, and the hypermutant samples that can dominate an ensemble.
Build catalogs with [Mutation catalogs](mutation-catalogs.html).

## The QC report

`ms_qc_report()` computes the per-sample QC table on a catalog. With a
signature set attached it also scores the pseudosignature faces; without
one it reports the burden and strand faces alone:

```{r qc-report}
ref <- ms_refdb_bundled()$SBS_GRCh38@matrices[[1]]
S   <- ref[, c(1, 5, 9)]
colnames(S) <- paste0("CS", 1:3)
E   <- matrix(c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2), 3, 16,
              dimnames = list(colnames(S), paste0("S", 1:16)))
sim <- ms_simulate(S, exposures = E, burden = 2000, seed = 2)

qc <- ms_qc_report(sim)
head(qc)
```

Each row is a sample: the burden columns (`total`, `log10_total`,
`burden_class`), the strand-bias faces, and (with signatures attached)
the artifact share with the specific technical signatures contributing.
`qc_flag` condenses the table into the per-sample verdict your pipeline
can filter on.

## The sibling sentries

The report is the composite; the **sentries** are the individual faces,
exposed so a pipeline can consume exactly one claim without recomputing
the rest:

```{r sentries}
qb <- ms_qc_burden(sim)
qb

qs <- ms_qc_sentries(sim)
qs
```

`ms_qc_mechanism_channels()` exposes the channel-level mechanism roster —
which channels each certified mechanism (APOBEC, tobacco, UV, and the
rest of the roster) is read from. It is the reference table behind the
mechanism columns above, and is also useful standalone when you want to
reason about channel subsets:

```{r mechanism}
mc <- ms_qc_mechanism_channels()
head(as.data.frame(mc))
```

`plot_qc_dashboard()` and `plot_pseudosig_contribution()` render the
report's faces (shown in
[the visualization gallery](visualization-gallery.html)).

## Hypermutant stratification

A handful of extreme-burden samples can drive an entire ensemble. The
stratifier splits the cohort into a hypermutant class and a regular
class — by a data-driven cutoff or a manual burden threshold — so the two
arms can be extracted, fitted, and reported separately:

```{r stratify}
strat <- ms_stratify_hypermutants(sim, manual_cutoff = 3000, seed = 1)
strat
```

The result is an `MsStratification` carrying the class assignment and the
cutoff used; `plot_hypermutator_burden()` draws the burden distribution
with the cutoff
([the visualization gallery](visualization-gallery.html)).

## Downsampling

Burden drives most QC verdicts, so a useful question is: how does the
analysis behave at lower sequencing depth? `ms_downsample()` thins a
catalog to a target per-sample total — the primitive behind the
calibration sanity protocol of
[Calibrated statistics](calibrated-statistics.html), and a useful robustness
check in its own right:

```{r downsample}
ds <- ms_downsample(sim, depth = 800, seed = 1)
range(colSums(ds@counts))
```
